title: Simulating Multi-Stakeholder Decision-Making with Generative Agents in Urban Planning

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing agent voting scores and reasoning keyword frequencies for urban planning proposals across experimental setups with and without demographic variables (e.g., age, gender, race, ethnicity) included in the agent prompts.

Analyzing the variance in project ratings (altruism-driven low-income housing vs. interest-driven shopping mall) and keyword usage among agents assigned distinct socioeconomic roles and life values (e.g., Low-Income Advocacy, Property Developer, Local Business).

bias_targets.target: Emergent multi-agent bias (Opinion convergence and Polarization)
bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating shifts in the variance of agent rating distributions and reasoning keyword frequencies before and after simulated group communication to detect echo-chamber effects, polarization, and artificial opinion convergence.
